mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are not positively correlated with low FEDFUNDS levels.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts suggests economic expansion, which may boost S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment may indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment rises but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in industrial production may signal economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in unemployment and payroll employment may indicate labor market contradictions, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both series rise but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising real consumer spending alongside low federal funds rates may indicate strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS rises and FEDFUNDS is low but returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rates may indicate tight monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4% but returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth in late expansion may signal impending slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDP grows but returns are positive.
